To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of low impact dyes in combination with biosalts in dyeing of organic cotton knitted fabrics will result in effluents with lower COD, BOD, TDS and hence better ecological performance.
the use of low impact reactive dye and biosalt in dyeing of organic cotton single jersey fabric has a significant effect on the reduction of COD, BOD, and TDS in dyeing effluents.

the use of low impact reactive dYES and the replacement of inorganic salt with biosalt in the exhaust dyeing of scouted and mercerized organic cotton single jersey fabric will reduce the COD, B0D and TDS value of the effluent and hence will improve the ecological performance of the dye bath.

the use of low impact reactive d yes in the dyeing of organic cotton fabrics and the use of biosalt in the place of inorganic salt in dyeing process.
the development of a new dyeing method for organic cotton knitted fabric using low impact dyes and biosalt in the presence of a cationic surfactant.
the use of biosalt and low impact reactive dye in dyeing of organic cotton knitted fabrics and its effect on the ecological parameters of effluent obtained.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of low impact dyes in the dye bath with biosalt as replacement for the regular inorganic salt is more environmentally friendly and has a greater ecological advantage.
the use of low impact reactive dye along with biosalt in the place of inorganic salt is the best option for the dyeing of organic cotton knitted fabrics.
the use of low impact dyes and biosalt in place of inorganic salt is a better option in terms of ecological parameters of the dye effluent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of biosalts in dye bath can be considered as a good alternative to the conventional inorganic salt in the dye bath and the use of low impact reactive dye is a good choice for dyeing organic cotton knitted fabrics.

the use of biosalt as a replacement for the inorgainc salt in the dyeing process is an effective way to reduce the chemical oxygen demand of the effluent but it would also increase the biological oxygen demand of the dyeing effluent.
the use of low impact dyes and biosalt in the place of the inorganic salts would be a more ecological approach for dyeing of organic cotton knitted fabric.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of biosalt in dye bath can reduce the chemical oxygen demand and total dissolved solids in the effluent considerably, which is a major advantage for the environment.
it is possible to achieve a more sustainable dyeing process by using low impact reactive dye and biosalt in the process.
the use of low impact reactive dye and biosalt can be used to reduce the ecological burden of the dye effluent.
